source.name: Fact Sheet #38: Substantial Rehabilitation, FS-38 (06/2025) (NYS Homes and Community Renewal)

rules.what: A building leaves rent stabilization as substantially rehabilitated only if DHCR finds, on the totality of the circumstances, that at least 75% of building-wide and apartment systems were replaced, the work began in a substandard or seriously deteriorated building (not required for space converted from nonresidential use), and all systems meet code, with the certificate of occupancy submitted.
For work started on or after January 1, 2024, the owner must apply to DHCR within one year after the work is completed and get a DHCR determination confirming the exemption.

rules.rule: No exemption after arson or harassment
rules.what: DHCR will not find a building was substandard or seriously deteriorated if the owner tried to get a vacancy through arson that led to a criminal conviction of the owner or agent, or if DHCR or another government body found harassment.

Occupied rent-regulated apartments that were not rehabilitated stay rent regulated until they are vacated, even when the rest of the building is found substantially rehabilitated. A tenant who was ordered out for hazardous conditions, or asked to move out temporarily for the work without giving up the apartment, keeps the protection when the apartment is habitable again.
When stabilized apartments are combined, the combined apartment is rent stabilized and its legal rent equals the combined legal rents of the original apartments.

terms.def: A DHCR finding that a building was rebuilt from a seriously deteriorated condition, with at least 75% of its systems replaced, which exempts it from rent stabilization. A final DHCR order is binding on the whole building, including later tenants, unless obtained through owner or agent fraud.
